The City’s Historic Preservation Program project team will present a history of the program

Survey) and an introduction to Phase 3: Historic Preservation Ordinance.

SUBJECT:  Presentation Regarding the City's Historic Preservation Program

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:

As part of the City Council's Strategic Plan to undertake the preservation of notable structures
and following a series of community outreach and workshops, on July 13, 2020, staff presented
a Historic Preservation Program to the City Council that included the preparation of a Historic
Context Statement (Phase 1 ); a survey of potentially historic properties (Phase 2); and
development of a Historic Preservation Ordinance (Phase 3). Phase 1 was completed in March
2022, and on September 26, 2022, the City Council awarded a contract to Historic Resources
Group ("HRG") for Phases 2 and 3 of the Historic Preservation Program.

In November of 2023, HRG completed its work on Phase 2, by finalizing a comprehensive survey
of potentially historic resources in the City that was received and filed by the City Council on May
13, 2024. The Historic Resources Survey was prepared on the basis developed in the Historic
Context Statement and provides a solid baseline of information about the built environment in
Alhambra. The Historic Context Statement and the Historic Resources Survey will be used for the
development of a Historic Preservation Ordinance. The Historic Resources Survey is a
comprehensive citywide survey in Alhambra. Properties identified as significant in the survey
report represent recommendations of potential eligibility only, pending the potential development
of a local ordinance and formal adoption by the City Council. In total, 865 properties were identified
as potentially eligible for listing at the federal, state, or local levels, either individually or as
contributors to potential historic districts. No potential historic resources were formally designated
as part of this survey. Phase 3 of the project involves drafting, reviewing, and adopting a new
Historic Preservation Ordinance.

At the Commission meeting, HRG will provide a presentation summarizing work completed during
Phases 1 and 2, and provide a project update for Phase 3. HRG will also review the anticipated
project schedule, opportunities for public input, and next steps. Lastly, HRG will provide general
overview and introduction of Phase 3 efforts.

Public outreach to the community will include direct mailings to property owners listed in the
survey, social media postings, and district meetings in all five (5) City Council districts during
October/November. The draft of the preservation ordinance, along with a questionnaire, will be
released on September 26, 2024. This will allow time for the community and Commission to
review the draft Ordinance and respond to the questionnaire. Questionnaires will be accepted
through November 18, 2024. Community input is welcomed and encouraged throughout the draft
ordinance process. Following public outreach, the Commission will reconvene, consider, and
discuss the draft preservation ordinance on December 4, 2024 and at future meetings as needed.

  AGENDA
  ITEM 1:  HISTORIC  PRESERVATION  COMMISSION  ROLES  AND
  RESPONSIBILITIES
  •  This is a report to inform the Historic Preservation Commission
  about their role and responsibilities; the Brown Act for open
  meetings for local legislative bodies in California; FPCC Conflict
  of Interest; and Rosenberg’s Rules of Order.
  •  Recommended Action: It is recommended that the Historic

  AGENDA
  ITEM 2:  HISTORIC PRESERVATION PROGRAM

  a history of the program phases (Phase 1: Historic Context
  Statement and Phase 2: Citywide Historic Resources Survey) and
  an introduction to Phase 3: Historic Preservation Ordinance.
  •  Recommended Action: It is recommended that the Historic
  Preservation Commission receive and file this informational

  sub-consultant, Architectural Resources Group (ARG),
  provided the presentation on the Historic Preservation Program.

  the  discussion  is  available  here:

G.  PUBLIC COMMENTS/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS:

  •  Jennifer Ng noted her appreciation for the City’s Historic Preservation efforts and
  discussed the need for interim protections for properties identified in the City’s
  Historic Resources Survey. Ms. Ng also discussed the urgency of adopting an
  Historic Preservation Ordinance. Ms. Ng also explained the process of
  incorporating an eighth potentially eligible historic district into the Historic
  Resources Survey and discussed the significance of the property at 203 South
  Cordova Street. (8:17 P.M.)

  •  Gabriel Ramirez congratulated the commissioners on their appointments and
  noted the importance of protecting historic sites and areas within the City. Mr.
  2
  09/25/2024
   Ramirez expressed his willingness to collaborate on research of public records
  related to historic sites. (8:24 P.M.)

  •  Todd Jones commented on the historic architecture in the City of Pasadena and
  the City of Pasadena’s preservation efforts. Mr. Jones expressed support for
  Alhambra’s preservation efforts but noted his disappointment in the number of
  individual properties and districts identified in the City’s Historic Resources Survey.
  (8:25 P.M.)

  •  Olga Michaels expressed her appreciation for the City’s Historic Preservation
  efforts and asked what the process would be to implement a moratorium applicable
  to properties identified in the City’s Historic Resources Survey. Ms. Michaels also
  noted her desire that the City utilize the Historic Resources Survey to protect
  homes and neighborhoods. (8:31 P.M.)

  •  Andrew Salimian expressed his support for the City’s Historic Preservation efforts
  and thanked the City’s consultants, HRG and ARG. Mr. Salimian noted the
  importance of preservation in mitigating change and offered assistance in
  promoting the current effort. (8:33 P.M.)

  •  Chris Olson noted the historic moment of the first Historic Preservation
  Commission meeting, discussed the founding of the Alhambra Historical Society,
  and expressed thanks for the City’s Historic Preservation efforts. Ms. Olson also
  commented on an upcoming Alhambra Historical Society event and their efforts to
  promote community participation and discussion on the Historic Preservation
  Ordinance. Ms. Olson commented on the informational notice sent out to owners
  and occupants identified in the City’s Historic Resources Survey. (8:36 P.M.)

  •  For additional information regarding the discussion, the audio recording of
  the  discussion  is  available  here:

  September-25-2024-Audio
